root_cause.text: In netfilter's nfnl_cthelper_dump_table(), the restart logic was placed after the hash-bucket for-loop, so if the saved "last" helper in cb->args[1] was deleted between dump rounds, a goto back into the loop body reused cb->args[0] after it had reached nf_ct_helper_hsize, bypassing the loop bounds check and reading past nf_ct_helper_hash.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that when the saved helper is deleted, "cb->args[1] is never cleared" and "The for loop finishes with cb->args[0] == nf_ct_helper_hsize, and the 'goto restart' jumps back into the loop body bypassing the bounds check, causing an 8-byte out-of-bounds read"; the patch fixes this by moving the `if (cb->args[1]) { cb->args[1] = 0; goto restart; }` block from after the loop to inside the loop body.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict the `cb->args[1]` restart path to the intended enclosing block so table dumping only restarts in the correct iteration context.
intent_record.what: The conditional block `if (cb->args[1]) { cb->args[1] = 0; goto restart; }` was moved inside the surrounding block by deleting a closing brace before it and adding the closing brace after it, changing its nesting and execution scope.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the restart logic now executes only while still inside the enclosing iteration/control block instead of unconditionally after that block ends, preventing the function from resetting `cb->args[1]` and jumping to `restart` outside the intended context.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the faulty restart/goto scope in nfnl_cthelper_dump_table() by limiting the cb->args[1] restart path to the proper loop context, which addresses the out-of-bounds iteration caused when the saved helper was deleted between dump rounds.

candidates.rationale: This jump performs the restart after the enclosing hash-bucket loop has already finished. If cb->args[1] refers to a helper deleted between dump rounds, control jumps back into the loop body while reusing cb->args[0] after it has advanced to nf_ct_helper_hsize, bypassing the normal loop bounds check and enabling out-of-bounds access.

This condition gates the misplaced restart logic outside the intended iteration scope. Triggering it after the loop completes causes the stale restart path that re-enters with an exhausted cb->args[0], leading to the out-of-bounds traversal described in the root cause.

This is part of the faulty restart sequence that clears the restart marker immediately before jumping back into the loop body from the wrong scope. While not the bounds bypass itself, it is directly involved in the vulnerable control flow.

vuln_statements.explanation: This jump is the direct control-flow flaw. It is executed from a restart block placed after the hash-bucket for-loop, so if the saved helper was deleted between dump rounds, execution jumps back into the loop body after cb->args[0] has already advanced to nf_ct_helper_hsize, bypassing the loop bound check and causing out-of-bounds access to nf_ct_helper_hash.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully visible in `nfnl_cthelper_dump_table()`. The function iterates buckets with `for (; cb->args[0] < nf_ct_helper_hsize; cb->args[0]++) {` and defines label `restart:` inside that loop body, just before `hlist_for_each_entry_rcu(cur, n, &nf_ct_helper_hash[cb->args[0]], hnode)`. After the `for` loop completes, it executes `if (cb->args[1]) { cb->args[1] = 0; goto restart; }`. This exactly matches the vulnerable construct: the restart logic is placed after the bucket loop, and the `goto restart` jumps back into the loop body reusing `cb->args[0]` without re-checking `cb->args[0] < nf_ct_helper_hsize`. If `cb->args[0]` has already reached `nf_ct_helper_hsize` and the saved `last` helper in `cb->args[1]` was deleted between dump rounds, the code can evaluate `&nf_ct_helper_hash[cb->args[0]]` out of bounds. There is no fix present here, because the restart handling is not guarded by a fresh bounds check and remains located after the `for` loop.
